# Cases that do not match CPython jinja2, with the reason.
#
# This file is an admission, not a waiver. A case listed here that starts
# passing fails the conformance test, so the list can only shrink deliberately.
# Anything not listed must match exactly.

# --- not gradable -------------------------------------------------------------
# Marked "ungradable": jinja2 does not pass this either. It prints a generator's
# memory address, which differs between two runs of the same interpreter, so
# there is no answer to match. Cases marked this way are reported separately and
# left out of the conformance rate, because a case nothing can pass is not a
# measure of anything.
minijinja/opfilters_txt.jj2              ungradable: jinja2 prints a generator's address

# --- Python object introspection ----------------------------------------------
# The two that are left of jinja2's sandbox-escape regression tests.
#
# __class__ is implemented -- it is a statement about gojja2's own value model,
# and inert. These two go further, into a Python object graph that has no
# counterpart in Go: the list of a class's subclasses, and the chain from a
# bound method to the interpreter's builtins. Matching them would mean building
# a decoy of the escape route the tests exist to document. See
# docs/divergences.md.
jinja-harvest/security_ad3b7dd838.jj2     # __class__.__subclasses__()
jinja-harvest/security_ccdfed5fc2.jj2     # __builtins__[__import__]

# --- lazy sequence filters ----------------------------------------------------
# Real model templates that hit the documented generator/list fork: DeepSeek-R1
# writes `{{ tools | map(attribute='function') | tojson(indent=2) }}`, and
# jinja2's map returns a generator, which json.dumps refuses. The template is
# broken under CPython jinja2 and renders under gojja2. See docs/divergences.md,
# "Lazy sequence filters".
chat-templates/models_llama-cpp-deepseek-r1__tool_call.jj2   # map()|tojson: generator is not JSON serializable
chat-templates/models_llama-cpp-deepseek-r1__tools.jj2       # map()|tojson: generator is not JSON serializable

# --- generator addresses (not gradable) ---------------------------------------
# `{{ [] | items }}` and friends: jinja2's items is lazy, so printing it renders
# a generator's repr, which embeds a memory address that differs between two
# runs of the same interpreter. Nothing can match these, gojja2 included, so
# they are reported apart from the rate rather than counted against it.
minja/syntax_2470465c79.jj2   ungradable: jinja2 prints a generator's address
minja/syntax_abd817f094.jj2   ungradable: jinja2 prints a generator's address
minja/syntax_decfafe0b4.jj2   ungradable: jinja2 prints a generator's address

# --- a constant that folds to an infinity --------------------------------------
# jinja2 writes a folded constant into its generated Python as that constant's
# repr, and repr(float("inf")) is `inf`, which is not a literal -- so the
# template raises NameError at run time. It only bites when the constant is
# emitted as *code*: `{{ 1e400 }}` prints "inf" because the output folder
# converts it to text first, while `{% if 1e400 %}` and `{% set x = 1e400 %}`
# raise.
#
# gojja2 renders the template. Reproducing the other answer would mean carrying
# a poisoned constant through the optimizer so that using it raises a NameError
# about a Python identifier that has no counterpart here.
own/fold/infinite_constant.jj2   # jinja2 writes `inf` into its generated source

# --- the width limit on computed integers -------------------------------------
# gojja2 refuses a computed integer wider than 2**20 bits; CPython computes it
# and answers. The bound itself is the divergence, and it is what stops a
# squaring loop -- which doubles the width each time -- from exhausting the
# machine with the output and iteration budgets both set. See docs/limits.md.
own/limits/integer_width_multiply.jj2   # gojja2 bounds a computed integer at 2**20 bits
own/limits/integer_width_power.jj2      # gojja2 bounds a computed integer at 2**20 bits

# --- a macro with a repeated parameter name -----------------------------------
# Both refuse the template; only the wording differs. jinja2 compiles a macro to
# a Python function, so a duplicate parameter reaches the Python compiler, and
# the SyntaxError it raises names `l_1_a` -- the identifier jinja2 generated --
# and a line of the generated module. Neither exists here, so gojja2 raises its
# own TemplateSyntaxError naming the parameter the template wrote.
#
# This was a *behavioural* divergence until the macro was refused: gojja2
# compiled it and the later parameter won, so a macro written here failed when
# the template was run under CPython. See docs/divergences.md.
own/macro/duplicate_parameter.jj2   # same refusal, different wording: jinja2 names a generated identifier

# --- a builtin type's generic alias -------------------------------------------
# Python 3.9 made a builtin type subscriptable as a *type annotation*, so
# `dict['k']` is a types.GenericAlias whose repr is `dict['k']`, not a lookup.
# jinja2's attribute fallback turns `dict.nosuch` into one too. gojja2's `dict`
# global is a callable that builds a dict, and nothing here models generic
# aliases, so all three are undefined. Calling it is identical in both, and
# only a handful of builtins accept the form -- `range['k']` raises in CPython
# as well, and is graded. See docs/divergences.md.
own/divergence/dict_subscript_str.jj2    dict['k'] is a generic alias in Python 3.9+
own/divergence/dict_subscript_int.jj2    dict[0] is a generic alias in Python 3.9+
own/divergence/dict_attr_fallback.jj2    dict.nosuch falls back to a generic alias

# --- self is iterable ---------------------------------------------------------
# TemplateReference defines __getitem__ and nothing else, which Python's legacy
# iteration protocol accepts, so `iter(self)` succeeds and the test says True.
# Iterating it raises either way; this is the one shape that answers instead of
# failing. See docs/divergences.md.
own/divergence/self_is_iterable.jj2      the legacy iteration protocol accepts __getitem__
own/divergence/self_list.jj2             list(self) asks for index 0 and raises KeyError

# --- a `{% set %}` block writing to a name that was never set ------------------
# The block form is an item assignment, not a namespace write -- jinja2 emits no
# isinstance check for it -- so both engines raise TypeError here. jinja2's
# generated code still holds the sentinel its resolver returns for an unknown
# name, because nothing has read it, so the message names `_MissingType`: a
# private class of jinja2's implementation with no counterpart here. gojja2 names
# what it actually holds. Every other target type matches exactly, dict and
# namespace included. See docs/divergences.md.
own/errors/nsref_block_undefined.jj2   # jinja2 names its own resolver sentinel

# --- the method resolution order ----------------------------------------------
# `__class__` is implemented and inert: a class object here has a name, a repr
# and equality, and nothing that leads anywhere. `__mro__` is the first step of
# the walk from a value to the interpreter's builtins, which is the escape route
# the two sandbox tests above document, so it belongs with __subclasses__ rather
# than with __class__. See docs/divergences.md.
own/divergence/class_mro.jj2   # __mro__ leads where __subclasses__ leads

# --- a class object as a type annotation ---------------------------------------
# Python 3.9 made `list` and `dict` subscriptable as a type annotation, so
# `[1].__class__['a']` is the generic alias `list['a']` on CPython. gojja2 models
# no generic aliases, exactly as it does not for the `dict` global above. jinja2's
# attribute fallback puts `.a` in the same position. See docs/divergences.md.
own/divergence/class_generic_alias_item.jj2    # list['a'] is a generic alias
own/divergence/class_generic_alias_slice.jj2   # so is list[slice(...)]
own/divergence/class_generic_alias_attr.jj2    # .a falls back to ['a']

# --- a type object's unbound methods --------------------------------------------
# A class carries its own methods, and calling one without an instance is a
# TypeError that names the method: "unbound method dict.items() needs an
# argument". gojja2's type object answers the attributes a class has *as a class*
# and refuses the rest, so it says there is no such attribute. That is the line
# __mro__ sits on -- an unbound method is a route back into the object model,
# where an int built by calling a class is an ordinary value. See
# docs/divergences.md.
own/divergence/class_unbound_dict_items.jj2                 # dict.items() unbound
own/divergence/class_unbound_dict_items_through_dictsort.jj2  # and through a filter
own/divergence/class_unbound_dict_items_through_xmlattr.jj2   # and another
own/divergence/class_unbound_str_upper_with_self.jj2        # str.upper('a') is 'A'
own/divergence/class_unbound_str_upper_without_self.jj2     # without one it names the method
own/divergence/class_unbound_list_append_with_self.jj2      # list.append([], 1) works
own/divergence/class_unbound_method_is_a_value.jj2          # and the method itself has a repr
own/divergence/class_unbound_method_is_defined.jj2          # so `is defined` is true
